value.body: A two-year master's degree covering analog and digital circuits, microprocessors and embedded systems, communication, VLSI basics and instrumentation, with lab work and a project. It leads to electronics industry roles, research and college teaching.

value.title: How you get in
value.body: A B.Sc with Electronics (some universities also accept Physics with Mathematics). Admission is through CUET-PG, a state or university entrance test, or graduation merit, depending on the university.

value.title: At a glance
items: Fewer universities offer it than M.Sc Physics or Chemistry, so check where it is offered.
Industry roles include embedded, testing and service work; some employers prefer B.Tech graduates for design roles.
College teaching needs NET (Electronic Science is a UGC-NET subject), SET or a PhD.

value.title: Postgraduate enrolment in Electronics
value.note: Counts PG students in the Electronics discipline under Science (mainly M.Sc); Electronics Engineering (M.Tech/M.E.) is a separate row and not included. AISHE counts only responding institutions, and coverage varies by year, so part of any change can reflect reporting rather than real growth or decline.
value.source: AISHE 2021-22, 2022-23 and 2023-24, Table 13 postgraduate enrolment by discipline, based on actual responses (Ministry of Education)
